content.comment_body: Hello all, I've recently started working with [product_name] software and a [product_name] module. Lately, I'm facing issues connecting my PC to the module via Ethernet. Interestingly, I was able to upload programs several times before, with no changes made and a confirmed working cable. The module's indicator is green but occasionally flashes yellow. Usually, I can't stop the module because the connection is lost. I am using [product_name] version [version_no] and the software version [version_no]. My network adapter and IP settings are as follows: Wireless LAN shows IPv6 and various IPv4 addresses with different subnets, while Ethernet has an autoconfiguration IPv4 address on a separate subnet. Any advice?
A screenshot of the error is available below.
First, ensure the project for the [version_no] device is set up correctly within the Network Project tab.
Next, add the necessary [product_name] module along with its network parameters.

Thanks [user_name]. I've already completed those steps. I checked another solution for a similar problem, but it did not help. To troubleshoot, I first checked my PC's IP using [product_name] instead of the ipconfig command. This is done by right-clicking on the PC icon in the Network Project section.

I then switched to Diagram Mode and accessed the Interface tab. I removed the Target IP address entry and clicked the blue refresh arrow. The system found a reachable [product_name] module with a specific IP, and using the Test function showed a successful connection.

Hello, Based on your error, the device is not on the same subnet as your PC. For example, your PC IP is 169.254.178.7 while your device IP is 192.168.3.110. Solution 1: Change your module IP address to match the PC subnet (e.g., 169.254.178.xxx, such as 169.254.178.10). Solution 2: Change your PC IPv4 address to match the device's subnet (e.g., 192.168.3.xxx, such as 192.168.3.2). See the attached reference. Good luck.
I have changed the module's IP address or the software did it automatically. For my setup, I have to clear the IP address each time and repeat the detection—otherwise, the connection fails.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered connectivity issues between their PC and a [product_name] device over Ethernet. Initial successful uploads were followed by failures, with module status lights indicating possible connectivity issues. Investigation showed mismatched subnets between the PC and module, requiring manual IP reconfiguration for communication. The configuration process within [product_name] software would often forget IP settings, prompting repeated manual adjustments.
analysis.user_expectations: User desires consistent and reliable Ethernet communication between their PC and [product_name] device for programming, ideally with automatic IP configuration and device detection that does not require manual intervention every time.
